clue.text: Surrealist is one artist among lots

indicators.note: among says one piece sits in the middle of the other

parts.note: lots means many
RA, a Royal Academician, is one artist

explanation.surface: A Surrealist painter is just one artist among a great many.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' signals the containment. Man Ray was an American Surrealist photographer and painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Man Ray was a leading figure of the Surrealist movement, so he is an example of a Surrealist.

clue.text: Dull, right? Just like a married woman

parts.note: mat (or matt) means dull, without shine
just means only

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether being dull is simply what a married woman is like.
explanation.definitionFit: Matronly describes the staid, dignified manner associated with a mature married woman, a matron.

clue.text: Sister nobody's heard of

indicators.note: heard of says the word for nobody is taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: nobody means none; the 's is just the possessive of the surface

explanation.surface: A nun is a sister of whom nobody has ever heard.
explanation.walkthrough: NONE, said aloud, sounds like NUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A nun is a member of a religious order of women, addressed as Sister.

clue.text: Remarkable energy supporting a scholar

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece supporting another sits below it

parts.note: an MA, a Master of Arts, is a scholar
zing means energy or zest

explanation.surface: Something remarkable is the energy a scholar puts into backing up a point.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'supporting' puts ZING underneath A and MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazing and remarkable are synonyms, both meaning astonishing or worthy of notice.

clue.text: Composer has pipe after tea

indicators.note: after places the pipe word behind the tea word

parts.note: cha is an informal British word for tea
a brier (briar) is a tobacco pipe made from briar root

explanation.surface: A composer enjoys a smoke on his pipe once tea is over.
explanation.walkthrough: Emmanuel CHABRIER was a French composer, best known for the rhapsody España.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmanuel Chabrier was a nineteenth-century French composer, so the clue word names his profession.

clue.text: Dreadful time suffered by kid, without respite

parts.note: a dreadful time is hell
for, as in 'hell for someone', means suffered by
kid is soft leather made from a young goat's skin

explanation.surface: A child goes through a terrible ordeal that never lets up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' looks like a child; it is the leather. Read the pieces as 'hell for leather': a bad time endured by kid.
explanation.definitionFit: Hell for leather is an idiom for going flat out, at full speed with no let-up.

clue.text: As soldier, one's attached to one's rifle — that's sort of fitting

definitions.text: As soldier, one's attached to one's rifle
definitions.meaning: a soldier's blade fixed to the end of a rifle
a push-and-twist bulb or lens mount, as opposed to a screw fitting

explanation.surface: A soldier is devoted to his rifle, which seems appropriate.
explanation.definitionFit: A bayonet is a blade fixed to a rifle, and a bayonet fitting is a push-and-twist connector for bulbs and lenses.

clue.text: Pretend to be one's friend, taking chap in

parts.note: one gives I, the Roman numeral; the 's is a link

indicators.note: taking ... in says the friend word swallows the chap word
in completes 'taking in', the containment signal

parts.note: a mate is a friend
a chap is a person

explanation.surface: Someone pretends to be a friend in order to take a man in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking ... in' reads as deceiving someone, but here it signals one piece swallowing another.
explanation.definitionFit: To impersonate someone is to pretend to be them, copying their manner or identity.

clue.text: Venomous creature's warning is to cause nervousness

definitions.meaning: the buzzing sound a rattlesnake's tail makes

explanation.surface: A snake's warning signal is meant to make you nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattlesnake shakes its rattle as a warning, and to rattle someone is to make them nervous.

clue.text: Have lucky escape, as Tom comes to land

definitions.meaning: to come out of trouble well by good fortune
a tom is a male cat, and a falling cat lands upright

explanation.surface: A tomcat comes down to earth and has a lucky escape.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom is a male cat, not a man's name: cats famously land on their feet.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to emerge from difficulty unharmed by luck, and literally describes how a cat lands.

clue.text: Can criticise way music came out of this

parts.note: a can is a tin
to pan is to criticise harshly
an alley is a narrow way or passage

explanation.surface: Someone can disparage the road that popular music came from.
explanation.walkthrough: TIN PAN ALLEY was the New York district of popular-song publishers.
explanation.definitionFit: Tin Pan Alley was the hub of American popular-song publishing, so music literally came out of it.

clue.text: Prize catch

definitions.meaning: to bag or shoot game for the table

explanation.surface: A prize catch.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot is slang for a trophy cup, and to pot an animal is to catch or shoot it.

clue.text: Policeman whose payment is overdue?

definitions.meaning: British slang for the police or a police officer
an invoice that is past due is an aged account

explanation.surface: A police officer who has not been paid.
explanation.walkthrough: OLD BILL is British slang for the police; read literally it is an old, unpaid invoice.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Bill is British slang for the police, and an old bill is one long unpaid.

clue.text: Poor grading restricting one scholar's performance

indicators.note: restricting says the jumbled letters hem in the other pieces
poor signals that the letters of grading are badly arranged

parts.note: one gives I, the Roman numeral
SCH is an abbreviation for scholar; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A bad mark limits a student's showing in an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' rearranges the seven letters into DARGING; 'restricting' then has that jumble hold the other pieces just after its D.
explanation.definitionFit: Discharging a duty is performing it, so discharging can mean the performance of a task.

clue.text: Wild about urn being empty, after this?

definitions.text: Wild about urn being empty, after this?

indicators.note: about says the word for wild goes round the other piece

parts.note: feral means wild

indicators.note: an empty word loses its inside, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Mourners go wild over an empty urn once the service is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the containment. The whole clue hints at a rite after which the empty urn is filled with ashes.
explanation.definitionFit: After a cremation service the ashes go into the urn, which was empty before the ceremony.

clue.text: General isn't too bothered about so many killed in war

indicators.note: bothered signals that the letters are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A general is unmoved by heavy casualties in battle.
explanation.walkthrough: The LOST GENERATION is the young men killed in the First World War.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the generation of young men who died in great numbers in the First World War.

clue.text: Failed to maintain improvement, but pass, in a way

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, a way
time may pass, or elapse

explanation.surface: Someone backslid, yet got through, after a fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a way' looks like 'somewhat', but 'a way' is the road abbreviation and 'in' signals the containment.
explanation.definitionFit: To relapse is to fall back into illness or bad habits after getting better.

clue.text: Dead time of the year, with unoriginal entertainment

parts.note: the winter is the dead season, when nothing grows
stale means unoriginal or hackneyed

explanation.surface: A tired old show put on in the bleak midwinter.
explanation.walkthrough: The Winter's Tale is a Shakespeare play.
explanation.definitionFit: The Winter's Tale is a Shakespeare play, and a play is an entertainment.

clue.text: Put in envelope and transported, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: rapt means transported, carried away with delight

explanation.surface: A letter is sealed up and sent off.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wrapped is enclosed or covered, as a letter is put inside an envelope.

clue.text: Island displays part of Koran, including aid to prayer

indicators.note: including says the Koran word holds the other piece

parts.note: a sura is a chapter of the Koran
a prayer mat aids a Muslim at prayer

explanation.surface: An island displays a passage of scripture alongside prayer aids.
explanation.walkthrough: SUMATRA is a large island of Indonesia.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumatra is a large island in western Indonesia.

clue.text: One keeping apart from silly capers

indicators.note: silly signals that the letters are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to join in foolish antics.
explanation.definitionFit: A spacer is a device or person that keeps things separated by a set distance.

clue.text: People one wouldn't associate with a husband in the city

indicators.note: in says these pieces go inside the city

parts.note: Paris is the city

explanation.surface: A husband living in the city mixes with undesirable people.
explanation.definitionFit: Pariahs are outcasts, people shunned by society whom others avoid.

clue.text: Disposition to acquire a painting technique

parts.note: temper means disposition or temperament

explanation.surface: A temperament suited to learning an art method.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to acquire' is a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempera is a painting method using pigment bound in egg yolk.

clue.text: Life force pert girl's finally lacking

indicators.note: finally lacking says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a chit is a pert young girl; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A cheeky girl turns out to have no vitality.
explanation.definitionFit: Chi, in Chinese thought, is the vital energy that flows through living things.

clue.text: Salute offer to restore Venus de Milo?

definitions.meaning: a military drill position honouring an officer

definitions.text: offer to restore Venus de Milo?
definitions.meaning: the famous armless statue would be given back her limbs

explanation.surface: A salute and a gift to a famous armless statue.
explanation.walkthrough: The Venus de Milo statue lacks both arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Present arms is a rifle salute, and literally means giving arms, as the statue needs.

clue.text: Beetle climbs up stick

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing up means reading upwards, backwards

parts.note: a dor is a dung beetle

explanation.surface: A beetle crawls up a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A rod is a stick or slender pole.

clue.text: Strictness and coldness first off

indicators.note: first off says the word drops its opening letter

parts.note: frigidity means coldness

explanation.surface: Discipline and aloofness come first.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigidity means strictness, an unbending inflexibility of rules or attitude.

clue.text: Frank's fruit said to be so sweetly preserved

definitions.note: Frank's is read as Frank is, so the 's is a link

indicators.note: said to be says the word is taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: candied means preserved in sugar

explanation.surface: Frank's fruit is reputedly preserved in sugar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a name; it means open. CANDIED spoken sounds like CANDID.
explanation.definitionFit: Candid means frank, honest and outspoken.
